THE ARGUMENT
Four gaps connect actuator mechanics to neural-control experiments
Revision C · Ch. 1, research gaps and objectives

Allow 1 minute. Read the argument in chapter order: predict force across actuator lengths; predict the torque delivered through compliant routes; recover source-grounded sensory evidence; and connect neural circuits to mechanical models with representative verification. These are project-specific gaps, not claims that no related tools exist elsewhere. A research robot is the long-term goal. Each contribution needs its own evidence.

Sources: Revision C · Ch. 1, research gaps and objectives

SCOPE AND ATTRIBUTION
This dissertation adds models and tests to an existing robot program
Revision C · Ch. 1; Ch. 6, Model Conversion and Actuator Coupling
Existing anatomy and mechanisms
New route modeling and tests

1 minute. Credit the AARL body plan, Morrow’s earlier robot and the Li walker mechanics, Steele’s biomimetic knee, and Deng’s published controller. OpenSim supplies human anatomy and targets; MyoConverter supplies initial conversion; MuJoCo supplies physics; SNS-Toolbox supplies neuron and synapse formulations. My contributions include actuator characterization with collaborators, correction identification, route-design and testing work with collaborators, SADb curation and application, model repairs and audits, and graphical circuit/interface implementations. The 92-actuator model is a modeling scope, not a physical robot completed in this dissertation. Ask me to explain the specific change and evidence rather than implying I invented these packages.

Sources: Revision C · Ch. 1; Ch. 6, Model Conversion and Actuator Coupling

text: SENSORY AFFERENT DATABASE: USE AND LIMITS
SADb exposes classification coverage without supplying controller gains
Revision C · Ch. 5, Fig. sadb_pivot and Use in Neural-Controller Design
Tagged papers retain their experimental context

1 minute. A pivot cell counts tagged papers, not neurons or independent physiological observations. A paper can appear in more than one cell. Selecting a cell retrieves the underlying records. Afferent classes Ia, Ib, and II denote spindle-primary, tendon-organ, and spindle-secondary channels. Their properties depend on preparation and task. Source conditions, sign, and phase guide interpretation; translating them into robot encoders and gains remains an explicit design and verification step. AI-assisted drafting does not count as scientific curation without source checking. The corpus is uneven and not exhaustively classified.

Sources: Revision C · Ch. 5, Fig. sadb_pivot and Use in Neural-Controller Design

NEURAL SIMULATION: MOTIVATING LIMITATION
The initial AnimatLab controller used one rhythm generator for suspended stepping
Revision C · Ch. 6, The AnimatLab Bipedal Walker; Li (2017), Deng (2019), Bolen (2021)
Historical mechanical model
Original left-joint traces

1 minute. Morrow and I combined Li’s mechanics with Deng’s two-level controller. The initial controller had ONE rhythm generator controlling both sides and a separate pattern-formation layer. I added a passive toe joint. Suspended alternating activity and stepping-like movement preceded subsequent feedback and bilateral-RG extensions. Hand tuning did not achieve weight-bearing walking. Do not attribute this earlier result to the later two-RG network. The body view and left-joint traces are the historical AnimatLab reference images. The angle units are not explicit in the source capture, so no numeric amplitude is asserted or converted.

Sources: Revision C · Ch. 6, The AnimatLab Bipedal Walker; Li (2017), Deng (2019), Bolen (2021)

My interfaces connect existing mechanics and neural formulations

My additions repair and audit custom muscle paths and joint signs, couple the quasi-static BPA-force model, and implement editable Simulink blocks and circuit interfaces. NEURAL SIMULATION: VERIFICATION BOUNDARY
The bridge exchanges signals while full-network dynamics still disagree
Revision C · Ch. 6, Closed-Loop Model Coupling and capability table
Interface correctness and controller equivalence need separate tests

1 minute. The bridge was checked against independent Python integration with single-muscle activation, different control rates, and sensor readback. Readback is bit-exact over the scored window. The exported neural network drove all 92 actuators for 5 seconds. However, tonic drive caused the Simulink realization to settle while the NumPy reference oscillated. Transfer of tuned controller parameters remains unresolved. Do not generalize the rhythm-core agreement to the full network. Hardware deployment and unsupported walking remain future work.

CONCLUSIONS
The evidence supports static torque capacity and specific simulation interfaces
Revision C · Chs. 3–7; final flexor MATLAB reduction, 23 October 2026

1 minute. Return to the four original gaps. Force: supported by characterized lengths and isometric data. Torque: identified corrections improve held-out predictions and redesigned routes have physical tests. Sensory evidence: searchable, linked, partially curated literature resource. Neural tools: matched circuit and interface checks, with explicit full-network discrepancy. Neither static isometric capacity nor supported stepping demonstrates a walking robot. No harness-free walking exists in the program records.

Sources: Revision C · Chs. 3–7; final flexor MATLAB reduction, 23 October 2026

NEXT EXPERIMENTS
Matched-pressure tests and controller reconciliation are the next checks
Revision C · Ch. 7; Ch. 6, remaining limits
Close the measured gaps before transferring control to hardware

45 seconds. The next experiments address the uncertainty exposed by the results: matched-pressure torque holds over the range, and diagnosing numerical/network differences before transferring tuned control. The dashed hardware path in this existing pipeline is proposed. Do not present a Jetson deployment, completed valve dynamics, or whole-body walking as achieved. Physical pulley tests and simultaneous biarticular verification are future work.

Sources: Revision C · Ch. 7; Ch. 6, remaining limits
